claims_in_paper.claim_text: The UK Strategic Road Network carries approximately one-third of all road traffic and two-thirds of freight tonne-kilometres , yet its adaptive capacity to changing climate conditions is under strain.
Transport climate resilience research spans qualitative risk reviews and quantitative resilience methodologies , as well as simulation-based approaches.

The output of this framework is the return on investment of climate resilience improvement projects in the regional road networks in the studied area under different climate projection scenarios (See Section 3.5 for details).
For a credible estimation of the cost, we make the assumption that the distribution of types of damaged roads is the same as the distribution of all roads within the entire road network.
For example, for all minor damaged roads, the proportion of paved road length is consistent with the proportion of paved roads in the whole road network.
The framework enables benefit-cost analysis as well as incorporating climate projection scenarios for resilience investment analysis.

Among vulnerability and risk assessment frameworks, probabilistic approaches enable a more comprehensive view for decision-makers and provide the ability to incorporate various uncertainties and assess their impact on the risk and resilience of the road network (Tang et al., 2013; Zhang and Yao, 2019; Espinet et al., 2018; Liu et al., 2024).

Under this context, the Government of Haiti and the World Bank are working on the Resilient Urban Transport and Acces­ sibility Project (RUTAP) (The World Bank, 2022) a $120 million program to increase climate resilience in transport infrastructure in the departments of Nippes, Sud, Sud-est, Grand'Anse and Nord.
